name: cty-collection-functions
instr:
I'm putting the collection functions back into our copy of go-cty. In `cty/function/stdlib/collection.go` each `XxxFunc` keeps its `function.Spec`, but the stubbed `Type` and `Impl` bodies panic: `HasIndexFunc`, `IndexFunc`, `LengthFunc`, `ElementFunc`, `CoalesceListFunc`, `ContainsFunc`, `DistinctFunc`, `ChunklistFunc`, `FlattenFunc`, `KeysFunc`, `LookupFunc`, `MergeFunc`, `ReverseListFunc`, `SliceFunc`, `ValuesFunc` and `ZipmapFunc` (the plain Go wrappers just call them). Could you implement them? `Compact` is done and shows the style.

`valueRefineLengthResult` in `cty/value_ops.go` is stubbed too; `Value.Length` needs it for unknown collections.

The doc comment on each function is the contract, including its error messages, edge cases, and how unknowns and marks are handled; please follow them exactly, because callers depend on those details.

Please keep every exported name and signature unchanged; private helpers are up to you. I'll run the package's own tests, and the rest of the module's tests must keep passing.

In the non-test code you add, please avoid: new `init()` functions; the `syscall`, `golang.org/x/sys`, `os/exec`, `os/signal`, `plugin`, `embed`, `runtime/cgo`, `runtime/pprof`, `runtime/trace`, `testing` and `flag` packages, cgo, and `//go:linkname` or `//go:embed` directives; `os.Exit`, `os.StartProcess`, `os.FindProcess` and `runtime.Goexit`; reading `os.Args`, `os.Executable`, `/proc/self` or `runtime/debug` build info; caller or stack lookups (`runtime.
